tagline: The far end of a road that starts in New Haven.
intro: Route 69 begins in the Amity section of New Haven. North of Bristol it gives up being a main road and goes on as a secondary one into Burlington, as Milford Street, toward its end at Route 4 near the town center. The scenic part is about three miles of that last run, from Bradley Road to Saw Mill Road.

Burlington broke from Bristol in 1806 and once kept several clock-making shops. Many of its industries quit or moved off after the Farmington Canal opened in 1829. The state extended Route 69 up here only in 1962.

moments.title: Sessions Woods
moments.text: At 341 Milford Street the state keeps a 771-acre preserve for teaching wildlife management, and black bears are commonly seen along its trails.

moments.title: Burlington green
moments.text: In Burlington center, at Route 4 and the George Washington Turnpike, the Federal-style Brown Tavern of about 1809, built for a merchant and later kept as a tavern, faces the triangular green.
